narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

Clearer than yesterday; temperatures and winds little changed. Dry until evening showers, with thunder possible, peaking this evening. 30°C / 86°F high, 19°C / 67°F low. Sky mostly cloudy early as reported, partly cloudy at midday and mostly cloudy in the evening. Wind NE early and SSW at midday; gusts to 39 km/h (21 kt). UV index 9.4 (very high). Air quality 74 (moderate) at Ochieng' Avenue, Kisumu Central, the highest of 3 stations. As of 06:01, reports through 04:00: no rain; no thunder; high so far 21°C / 70°F; low so far 21°C / 70°F; peak sustained 11 km/h; sky mostly cloudy.

## Extended Outlook

Temperatures and winds much the same through Thursday, with showers and thunderstorms likely each day. Skies partly cloudy Tuesday and Wednesday, then mostly cloudy Thursday. Thursday's call: rain, 73%, with all four models wet; highs 29 to 31 °C. Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) calls it dry. At this lead ICON has the best record, right 77% of the time over 65 checks.

Further out, temperatures and winds much the same through Monday, with showers and thunderstorms likely Friday and Saturday, and showers and thunderstorms possible Sunday and Monday. Friday: all four models wet, highs around 29 °C. Saturday: all four models wet, highs 29 to 33 °C. Sunday: all three models that reach it wet, highs around 30 °C, thunder possible rather than likely.

Only GFS, ECMWF and ICON reach past Saturday. ECMWF, ICON and UKMO are the wetter solutions from Friday to Saturday; GFS keeps it drier. Monday's call: rain, 100%, with one of two models wet; highs around 29 °C. At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 77% of the time over 61 checks.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Convective instability today: UKMO 4030 J/kg, ICON 2110 J/kg, ECMWF 1550 J/kg and GFS 860 J/kg. Thunder likely; any thunderstorm brings sudden gusts well above the 39 km/h (21 kt) forecast.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Peak gust 28 km/h (15 kt). Any thunderstorm brings sudden gusts well above this figure; the water is unsafe while one is nearby.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1010 hPa) and highest toward the southeast (1015 hPa) — a 6 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. The lower pressure to the north is deepening over the next three days. Pressure is also falling toward the south, southeast — a large-scale feature building in that direction, though this sampling cannot say how fast or whether it will reach here. Pressure overhead is near-steady. Sampling is a nine-point ring at 12-degree spacing, so this locates a direction, not a centre or a front. Across the basin's 5 points, pressure today sits between 1012.6 and 1014.9 hPa, near-steady over three days (-0.3 hPa). Pressure here over the last 24 hours: -0.2 hPa.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

On rain the record ranks ICON first at Day+3, right 77% of the last 30 checks and ECMWF first at Day+7, right 77% of the last 30 checks. On today's high UKMO is the warmest model at 29.8 °C and GFS the coolest at 28.7 °C; the call's 30.2 °C sits at the warm end. At Day+0, no model is meaningfully better than the others here yet. At Day+7, ECMWF is the strongest rain caller here and GFS the weakest. At Day+0, Best Match slightly under-forecasts peak wind here.

Figures issued 06:01. Written by code; a discussion follows when a model answers.
